node.title: The Human Intelligence Debt Dilemma: A Game-Theoretic Account of Why Rational Agents Build Irrational Architectures
node.reading:
This document is a field notes paper : a structured conceptual contribution grounded in direct practitioner observation, prior to formal empirical validation. It extends the framework introduced in Human Intelligence Debt: A Socio-Technical Metric for Measuring the Human Cost of Imperfect Data Flows and developed in The Harvester Multiplication Problem . Readers unfamiliar with the core definitions — Human Intelligence Contribution Ratio (HICR), Human Intelligence Contribution Target (HICT), and Human Intelligence Debt (HID) — are encouraged to read those papers first. The next stage of this series will be a working paper developing the measurement methodology and a preregistered empirical research protocol; empirical results will follow instrument validation.

A Game-Theoretic Reading of Why Rational Agents Consistently Produce Irrational Architectures

Es una hipótesis de arquitectura, no un resultado del caso relojero. Hay economías reales de estandarización y el coste de transición confunde comparaciones tempranas.
The attribution ratchet sharpens one incentive mechanism behind architectural complexity: blame remains attached to the source while credit is captured downstream.
Es comparación entre mecanismos, no deducción de una teoría a partir de la otra ni explicación universal de la fragmentación.
The second-order HID programme can extend the incentive question by testing how contribution recognition and withdrawal rights change feasible collective outcomes.
HID2-01…10 están propuestos y no ejecutados; un toy algebraico no demuestra aceleración económica real.

For a complementary reading, see [Why rational agents can create irrational architectures](https://tegrity.ai/the-human-intelligence-debt-dilemma-a-game-theoretic-account-of-why-rational-agents-build-irrational-architectures/).
